exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 17–26, $$V$$ is a vector space and $$A$$ is an $$m \times n$$ matrix. Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The number of pivot columns of a matrix equals the dimension of its column space.
(T/F) The number of variables in the equation $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$$ equals the nullity $$A$$ .
(T/F) A plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ is a two-dimensional subspace of $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ .
(T/F) The dimension of the vector space $${\mathbb{P}}_{{}^{4}}$$ is $$4$$ .
(T/F) The dimension of the vector space of signals, $$\mathbb{S}$$ , is $$10$$ .
(T/F) The dimensions of the row space and the column space of $$A$$ are the same, even if $$A$$ is not square.
(T/F) If $$B$$ is any echelon form of $$A$$ , then the pivot columns of $$B$$ form a basis for the column space of $$A$$ .
(T/F) The nullity of $$A$$ is the number of columns of $$A$$ that are not pivot columns.

(T/F) If a set $$\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{\mathbf{p}} \right\}$$ spans a finite-dimensional vector space $$V$$ and if $$T$$ is a set of more than $$p$$ vectors in $$V$$ , then $$T$$ is linearly dependent.
(T/F) A vector space is infinite-dimensional if it is spanned by an infinite set.

The first four Hermite polynomials are $$1 \text{,} 2t \text{,} - 2 + 4t^{2}$$ , and $$- 12t + 8t^{3}$$ . These polynomials arise naturally in the study of certain important differential equations in mathematical physics.2 Show that the first four Hermite polynomials form a basis of $${\mathbb{P}}_{3}$$ .
The first four Laguerre polynomials are $$1 \text{,} 1 - t \text{,} 2 - 4t + t^{2}$$ , and $$6 - 18t + 9t^{2} - t^{3}$$ . Show that these polynomials form a basis of $${\mathbb{P}}_{3}$$ .

Let $$B$$ be the basis of $${\mathbb{P}}_{3}$$ consisting of the Hermite polynomials in Exercise 27, and let $$\mathbf{p}(t) = \text{7} - \text{12} t - \text{8} t^{2} + \text{12} t^{3}$$ . Find the coordinate vector of $$\mathbf{p}$$ relative to $$B$$ .

Let $$B$$ be the basis of $${\mathbb{P}}_{2}$$ consisting of the first three Laguerre polynomials listed in Exercise 28, and let $$\mathbf{p}(t) = \text{7} - 8t + \text{3} t^{2}$$ . Find the coordinate vector of $$\mathbf{p}$$ relative to $$B$$ .
Let $$S$$ be a subset of an $$n$$ -dimensional vector space $$V$$ , and suppose $$S$$ contains fewer than $$n$$ vectors. Explain why $$S$$ cannot span $$V$$ .
Let $$H$$ be an $$n$$ -dimensional subspace of an $$n$$ -dimensional vector space $$V$$ . Show that $$H = V$$ .
If a $$3 \times 8$$ matrix $$A$$ has rank $$3$$ , find nullity $$A$$ , rank $$A$$ , and rank $$A^{T}$$ .
If a $$6 \times 3$$ matrix $$A$$ has rank $$3$$ , find nullity $$A$$ , rank $$A$$ , and rank $$A^{T}$$ .
Suppose a $$4 \times 7$$ matrix $$A$$ has four pivot columns. Is $$\text{Col} A = {\mathbb{R}}^{4}?$$ Is $$\text{Nul} A = \mathbb{R}^{3}?$$ Explain your answers.
Suppose a $$5 \times 6$$ matrix $$A$$ has four pivot columns. What is nullity $$A$$ ? Is $$\text{Col} A = {\mathbb{R}}^{4}?$$ Why or why not?
If the nullity of a $$5 \times 6$$ matrix $$A$$ is $$4$$ , what are the dimensions of the column and row spaces of $$A$$ ?
If the nullity of a $$7 \times 6$$ matrix $$A$$ is $$5$$ , what are the dimensions of the column and row spaces of $$A$$ ?
If $$A$$ is a $$7 \times 5$$ matrix, what is the largest possible rank of $$A?$$ If $$5 \times 7$$ matrix, what is the largest possible rank of $$A?$$ Explain your answers.

If $$A$$ is a $$4 \times 3$$ matrix, what is the largest possible dimension of the row space of $$A?$$ If $$A$$ is a $$3 \times 4$$ matrix, what is the largest possible dimension of the row space of $$A$$ ? Explain.
Explain why the space $$\mathbb{P}$$ of all polynomials is an infinite-dimensional space.
Show that the space $$C(\mathbb{R})$$ of all continuous functions defined on the real line is an infinite-dimensional space.

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 43–48, $$V$$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space, and the vectors listed belong to $$V$$ . Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer. (These questions are more difficult than those in Exercises 17–26.)

problem.paragraph: (T/F) If there exists a set $$\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{\mathbf{p}} \right\}$$ that spans $$V$$ , then $$\dim V \leq p$$ .
(T/F) If there exists a linearly dependent set $$\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{\mathbf{p}} \right\}$$ in $$V$$ , then $$\dim V \leq p$$ .
(T/F) If there exists a linearly independent set $$\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{\mathbf{p}} \right\}$$ in $$V$$ , then $$\dim V \geq p$$ .
(T/F) If $$\dim V = p$$ , then there exists a spanning set of $$p + 1$$ vectors in $$V$$ .
(T/F) If every set of $$p$$ elements in $$V$$ fails to span $$V$$ , then $$\dim V > p$$ .
(T/F) If $$p \geq 2$$ and $$\dim V = p$$ , then every set of $$p - 1$$ nonzero vectors is linearly independent.
Justify the following equality: $$\dim{ \text{Row} }A + \text{nullity} A = n$$ , the number of columns of $$A$$
Justify the following equality: $$\dim \text{Row} A + \text{nullity} A^{T} = m$$ , the number of rows of $$A$$

exercise_group.instruction: Exercises 51 and 52 concern finite-dimensional vector spaces $$V$$ and $$W$$ and a linear transformation $$\left. T:V\rightarrow W \right.$$ .

problem.paragraph: Let $$H$$ be a nonzero subspace of $$V$$ , and let $$T(H)$$ be the set of images of vectors in $$H$$ . Then $$T(H)$$ is a subspace of $$W$$ , by Exercise 47 in Section 4.2. Prove that $$\dim T(H) \leq \dim H$$ .

Let $$H$$ be a nonzero subspace of $$V$$ , and suppose $$T$$ is a one-to-one (linear) mapping of $$V$$ into $$W$$ . Prove that $$\dimT(H) = \dim H$$ . If $$T$$ happens to be a one-to-one mapping of $$V$$ onto $$W$$ , then $$\dim V = \dim W$$ . Isomorphic finite-dimensional vector spaces have the same dimension.

[T] According to Theorem 12, a linearly independent set $$\{\mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{k}\}$$ in $${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ can be expanded to a basis for $${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ . One way to do this is to create $$A = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{v}_{1} & \ldots & \mathbf{v}_{k} & \mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{1}} & \ldots & \mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{n}} \end{bmatrix}$$ , with $$\mathbf{e}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{n}}$$ the columns of the identity matrix; the pivot columns of $$A$$ form a basis for $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Let $$\{\textbf{v}_{1}, \text{…} ,\textbf{v}_{p}\}$$ be a basis for $$H \cap K$$ . Notice $$\{\textbf{v}_{1}, \text{…} ,\textbf{v}_{p}\}$$ is a linearly independent subset of $$H$$ , hence by Theorem 12, $$\{\textbf{v}_{1}, \text{…} ,\textbf{v}_{p}\}$$ can be expanded, if necessary, to a basis for $$H$$ . Since the dimension of a subspace is just the number of vectors in a basis, it follows that dim $$(H \cap K) = p \leq \text{dim} H$$ .
